text:
Jordan: hey all :wave: quick q on keys — I set up my hosted API key from the console for a demo but when I try to run a local streaming test it drops mid-stream and I see 429s. Should I be using the sandbox key for local dev instead?
Sam (DevEx): Hi Jordan — welcome! For day-to-day local dev and CI you should use the sandbox key. Hosted keys are for demos / prod and have stricter rate buckets + IP policies. :+1:
Maya: fwiw if you need to demo a paid model briefly, use hosted but keep payloads small. Sandbox supports streaming too but with lower quota.
Jordan: thanks! is there a quick way to swap keys for a test script? currently my app reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env.
Sam (DevEx): yep — just export REDWOOD_API_KEY to the sandbox token. Example:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxx"
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Jordan: great. Alex — you mentioned IP whitelist could also affect streaming?
Alex: correct. If you're on hosted and your org has IP whitelisting enabled we may be rejecting chunked connections from dynamic dev IPs. Sandbox keys usually bypass org-level whitelists. If you need hosted access for dev, ask security to add your office/devbox IP.
Jordan: how do I ask for more sandbox quota? my local tests keep hitting a burst limit.
Sam (DevEx): open the internal request form (DevEx handles sandbox bumps): https://redwood.internal/devex/keys-requests OR email devex@redwood.ai with subject "Sandbox quota request" and include: team, rough qps, expected test duration.
Maya: also run with smaller batch_size and shorter max_tokens in tests to avoid burning quota quickly. Try batch_size=1 for streaming debug.
Jordan: any rules about storing keys in repos/CI?
Sam (DevEx): important: never commit keys. For CI use ephemeral CI service tokens from the console (there's a "CI token" flow) or the secrets manager. Hosted keys are considered sensitive — treat them like any secret.
Alex: if you hit 429s on sandbox, post the short trace (redacted) here and we can check the exact bucket/rates. Usually a backoff with jitter fixes transient 429s.
Jordan: thanks everyone — I'll swap to sandbox for local and file the form if I need a bump.
onboarding-bot: Welcome message: "Welcome to Redwood! Need anything else? Check the onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/onboarding and drop @Sam (DevEx) if stuck."
